title: Root-cause workflow for config-induced quality deltas
creator: Lina Foster
description:
Background: A recent production incident surfaced a quality regression that correlated with a model-serving config change (kv-cache/quant profile tweak). Existing smoke evals missed the delta because the failing signal was a narrow prompt distribution and a subtle ranking shift across a small customer cohort.

Goal: Define and implement a reproducible investigation and automated prevention workflow that links config/model changes to quality deltas and ensures: (1) fast attribution during incidents, (2) automated generation or selection of targeted evals for missed gaps, (3) PR gating + rollout guardrails for risky config changes, and (4) alerting integrated with the console and postmortem runbook.

Scope of work (high-level):
- Instrumentation: tag serving traces with config-sha and model-variant metadata, persist short-lived diffs for request cohorts (latency/score distributions).
- Attribution: build a small pipeline that correlates evaluation metric shifts with recent config/model commits and returns ranked candidate deltas (delta-score, affected-prompts).
- Synthetic test generation: take the identified affected-prompts and expand with paraphrases + edge-case variants to create targeted smoke tests that run in the canary and pre-merge CI.
- Eval harness improvements: add short-window cohort-based regression checks to the smoke suite and add golden-snapshot comparisons for ranking-sensitive tasks.
- PR gating & rollout policy: config PRs that change kv/quantization/kernel-selection must surface a delta risk score and (if above threshold) require a canary with targeted evals and hold rollout until regression cleared.
- Observability & alerts: wire regression detection to Console alerting (channel + incident page link) and create a quick triage dashboard with top-5 suspected config drivers.

Trade-offs considered:
- Running expanded targeted evals for every config change increases CI cost. We will tier checks: cheap paraphrase expansion in pre-merge, heavier generation only for changes affecting kernel selection / quant profiles.
- Attribution accuracy vs. speed: initial implementation will prioritize high-precision, narrow-scope heuristics (time-window + config-sha) to reduce false positives; later iterations will use probabilistic attribution models.

Success criteria:
- Time-to-attribution for regressions reduced to under 3 hours for config-linked incidents.
- At least 80% of incidents similar to the previous one automatically produce a targeted smoke test within 24 hours.
- No config rollout allowed to reach production with delta-risk > threshold without canary passing targeted evals.

Deliverables (concrete):
1) Confluence runbook "Config Delta Attribution & Prevention" with triage checklist and playbook links.
2) Lightweight attribution service prototype (logs->candidate deltas).
3) Targeted synthetic-test generator integrated into eval-harness.
4) CI gating rules and a Console UI flag for delta-risk per PR.

Owners: engineering (Maya Chen) for implementation, PM (Arjun Patel) for prioritization and release gating, Research (Sofia Morales) for eval design and paraphrase generation heuristics.

Open questions / blockers:
- Access to historical KV-cache traces in prod (security/compliance signoff required).
- Threshold definition for delta-risk (need PM + research to define metric).
- Cost budget for expanded CI evals (eng + infra alignment).

Next steps (this sprint):
- [Maya] prototype minimal attribution pipeline (logs + config-sha correlation) in a devstack by 2025-03-07.
- [Arjun] draft PR gating policy and threshold proposal by 2025-03-05.
- [Sofia] produce initial paraphrase expansion rules and a seed dataset for synthetic tests by 2025-03-10.

Links to artifacts: Confluence runbook (draft), prototype repo, and incident postmortem are linked below.
